posts.topic: Cress heads: a growing project for kids

kid.title: Cress heads
kid.blurb: Give an eggshell a funny face and grow green “hair” in a week.
need: An empty eggshell (or a clean yoghurt pot)
steps: Wash your hands. Ask a grown-up for a clean, empty eggshell or yoghurt pot.
Draw a funny face on the front with a pen.
Fill it with damp cotton wool. It should be wet but not dripping.
Sprinkle cress seeds on top and gently pat them down. Do not cover them.
Put it on a bright windowsill. Give it a few drops of water every day.
After 4 to 7 days your cress “hair” will be ready. Snip it with scissors and put it in a sandwich!
kid.fact: Cress seeds turn sticky when they get wet. That helps them cling to the cotton wool.
kid.adult_note: If you use an eggshell, use one from a boiled egg and wash hands afterwards. A clean yoghurt pot works just as well.

safety_lines: If you use an eggshell, use one from a boiled egg and wash hands afterwards. A clean yoghurt pot works just as well.
Stay close by. Little ones need a grown-up for scissors, hot things, knives and anything with sharp edges.

hook.hook: Nobody tells you November is still rhubarb planting time

captions.instagram:
Nobody tells you November is still rhubarb planting time

If you want to know how to grow rhubarb UK gardens thrive on, plant dormant crowns from November to March. Always pull and twist the stems at the base instead of cutting them, so you do not leave stumps that rot. Trim off the poisonous leaves and stew the stalks with sugar and orange juice for 10 minutes so nothing goes to waste.

Check your local frost dates.

12 ways to use up carrots before they go to waste

If you are wondering what to do with too many carrots, I like to twist off the tops and store them unwashed in boxes of damp sand for 4–6 months. You can also leave them in the ground under straw until early spring. Blanch sliced roots for 3 minutes before freezing to keep them handy for stews and soups.

Check your local frost dates.

hook.hook: Stop buying microgreens. Sow your own this November

Stop buying microgreens. Sow your own this November

I grow microgreens on a bright windowsill using a shallow tray. Keep the compost moist by misting or watering from below to avoid mould. If you want to learn how to grow microgreens UK style, re-sow every week or two for a continuous supply. Cut them with scissors just above the compost to top your eggs or toast.
